fullPassage:
For two days the wind and rain had all disappeared, and Martha came happily. 'You'll love the moor then, when it's full of flowers and birds!' 'I'd like to go outside,' said Mary. 'Well, why don't you? It's lovely! You've never done much walking, have you? I don't think you could walk five miles to our cottage!'
'But I'd like to meet your family,' said Martha happily.
Martha looked at the little girl for a moment. She remembered how Mary had been when she arrived. 'She's not friendly, is she,' Martha had thought. But she had decided to be kind. 'Miserable and disagreeable and kind — I wonder what Dickon will think of you!'
'Well, I've never,' said Martha. 'Dickon's my brother. He's twelve, and he's got a pony. He goes out on the moor to talk to the birds and animals, and they all know him.'
Martha had said, 'Goodbye, see you tomorrow.' Mary was outside. The gardens look different, and the change in the weather had even made Ben Weatherstaff different to talk to.
Just then Martha came running up to Mary, very excited. 'I've got something to tell you! I told Mother all about you. And she was very interested. She sent you a present!'
'A present for me!' She repeated. 'How could a family of fourteen hungry people give anyone a present?'
Mother bought it from the corner shop, and Mary stared at it. 'What is it?' she asked. 'Don't they have skipping-ropes in India?'
'That looks lovely,' said Mary. 'Your mother is very kind. Do you think I could ever like her if I ever met her?'
She took the rope and ran into the middle of the room. She counted up to a hundred.
She took the rope and ran into the garden. She jumped and counted. She ran along the paths. 'Stop outside and play in the fresh air!'

'Well, I've never,' said Martha. 'Dickon's my brother. He's twelve, and he's got a pony. He goes out on the moor to talk to the birds and animals, and they all know him.'
Martha had said, 'Goodbye, see you tomorrow.' Mary was outside. The gardens look different, and the change in the weather had even made Ben Weatherstaff different to talk to.
Just then Martha came running up to Mary, very excited. 'I've got something to tell you! I told Mother all about you. And she was very interested. She sent you a present!'
